facts.statement: A Soviet-Mongolian expedition discovered a Harpymimus skeleton in the Gobi Desert in 1981.
facts.quote: In 1981, a Soviet-Mongolian expedition uncovered a theropod skeleton in the Gobi Desert.

facts.statement: Harpymimus was named and described by Rinchen Barsbold and Altangerel Perle in 1984.
facts.quote: In 1984 this was named and shortly described by Rinchen Barsbold and Altangerel Perle as the type and only species of the new genus Harpymimus: Harpymimus okladnikovi.

facts.statement: The genus name Harpymimus means "Harpy mimic" and references the Harpy of Greek mythology.
facts.quote: The generic name Harpymimus is a reference to the fearsome Harpy of Greek mythology and derived from Greek ἅρπυια (harpyia), "Harpy", and μῖμος (mimos), "mimic".

facts.statement: The species name okladnikovi honors the Soviet archaeologist Alexey Pavlovich Okladnikov.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the late Soviet archeologist Alexey Pavlovich Okladnikov.

facts.statement: Harpymimus fossils were found in the Mid-Late Albian Shinekhudag Formation in the Eastern Gobi Province of Mongolia.
facts.quote: It was recovered in the Dundgovi Aimag (Eastern Gobi Province), from an exposure of the Shinekhudag Formation now part of the Khuren Dukh Formation which dates to the Mid-Late Albian

facts.statement: Harpymimus lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 130 to 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 130 a 125 millones de años entre el Hauteriviense y el Barremiense

facts.statement: Harpymimus retained teeth in its lower jaw, a trait absent in later ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: Unlike later, more derived ornithomimosaurs, Harpymimus still possessed teeth, although they appear to have been restricted to the dentary of the lower jaw.

facts.statement: Harpymimus likely used a beak on its upper jaw combined with lower jaw teeth to grasp and hold food.
facts.quote: There is evidence of a beak covering the upper jaw which, in concert with the dentary teeth, was likely employed for grasping and holding food.

facts.statement: Harpymimus had a long neck, long legs, and long arms with sharp grasping claws.
facts.quote: Its general appearance was much like that of later ornithomimosaurs (long-necked, long arms with sharp grasping claws, and long legs).

facts.statement: Harpymimus had at least ten to eleven cylindrical teeth per side in its lower jaw, separated by interdental plates.
facts.quote: The teeth of Harpymimus differ from those of another basal ornithomimosaur, Pelecanimimus polyodon, in that they are restricted to the dentary, are cylindrical and separated by interdental plates, and number at least ten and perhaps eleven per side.

facts.statement: Harpymimus's small teeth were likely used only for grabbing food, not for cutting or piercing.
facts.quote: The small teeth of Harpymimus were probably used only for grabbing and holding food items, unlike those of many other theropods, which were adapted to cutting or piercing prey.

facts.statement: Harpymimus had a skull approximately 262 mm long, which was less than half the length of its 600 mm neck.
facts.quote: The length of the skull is approximately 262 mm, more than twice its approximate height and less than half the length of the neck (approximately 600 mm).

facts.statement: Research suggests Harpymimus is more derived than Pelecanimimus but basal to the clade containing Garudimimus and Ornithomimidae.
facts.quote: In their 2005 paper, Kobayashi and Barsbold also conducted a detailed cladistic analysis of Harpymimus and determined that Harpymimus is basal to the clade of Garudimimus brevipes plus Ornithomimidae, yet is more derived than Pelecanimimus polyodon.

facts.statement: A 2020 phylogenetic analysis classified Harpymimus as a basal deinocheirid.
facts.quote: In the description of Paraxenisaurus from Serrano-Brañas et al. (2020), their phylogenetic analysis recovered Harpymimus to be a basal deinocheirid.

facts.statement: Harpymimus is one of only two known ornithomimosaurs that retained teeth, a primitive trait for the group.
facts.quote: Of all the known ornithomimosaurs, only Harpymimus and Pelecanimimus retained teeth, a trait which is primitive (plesiomorphic) for the clade Ornithomimosauria.

facts.statement: The type specimen's skull is virtually complete but badly crushed, hiding some anatomical details.
facts.quote: The skull of the type specimen of Harpymimus is virtually complete, but badly crushed, obscuring some anatomical detail.

facts.statement: The genus Harpymimus was named by Barsbold and Perle in 1984.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Harpymimus (genus), Barsbold and Perle 1984

facts.statement: Harpymimus belongs to the family Deinocheiridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Deinocheiridae

facts.statement: Harpymimus lived during the Albian stage, between 110.1 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Harpymimus has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

facts.statement: According to Kobayashi and Barsbold, Harpymimus is more derived than Pelecanimimus polyodon.
facts.quote: con todo es más derivado que Pelecanimimus polyodon

facts.statement: The analysis suggests that ornithomimosaurians later migrated to North America during or before the end of the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: y después emigraron a Norteamérica durante o en algún momento antes del finales del Cretácico
